Strategy · console surface planning · Netlify + Vercel

Ten more screens — what closing on Netlify and Vercel actually requires

Both competitor consoles held against our 51-surface build outline: which surfaces do they have that we never specified, which fit Barkpark's identity, and which are deliberate skips. Output: seven screens to request from the designer now (N-01…N-07, each mapped to a backend capability that exists or is wave-planned) and three concept sketches for the differentiators (N-08…N-10). Filter applied throughout: no Netlify/Vercel cosplay — a screen earns a request only if it serves the named-box, price-transparent, content-first identity. Companions: Vercel gap analysis · auto-deploy target UI.

Request from the designer now (N-01…N-07)

#ScreenModeled onWhy it clears the barBackend reality
N-01Logs viewer — instance tab + site drill-in: journal tail, Caddy access lines, level/source filter, follow modeVercel Logs / Netlify function logsBoth competitors treat logs as a core tab; we ship a box the user OWNS and still make them SSH for logs — the worst of both worldsAgent command allowlist already has logs (journalctl -n 200); Caddy access logs sit on-box; needs a streaming relay endpoint, no new infra
N-02Site settings — composed page: general (name, framework, scale mode), git, previews + protection, danger zone (delete)Vercel project settings / Netlify site settingsOur outline has the pieces (E-03/06/07, F-05) but no composed home; competitors prove settings-as-place matters for findabilityPure composition of existing PATCH endpoints
N-03Usage & cost dashboard (team-level) — meters × provider pricing = real €/month per instance, projected next invoice, per-site attributionVercel spend management — but honestThe identity flagship. Vercel projects usage-billing anxiety; we can show an actual server price. Nobody else in this market can render a true bill previewHetzner pricing catalog (EUR) + Azure retail cache (USD) already in the plane; 13 meters + quota model live; join is arithmetic
N-04Lock production — pin the published deploy: stop git-auto AND content-auto publishing until unlocked; banner explains what's heldNetlify "stop auto-publishing"Netlify's most-loved safety valve; ours is stronger because it also holds the content loop (publish-gated batching from the gap paper's wave 3)Prototype already carries a publishMode prop; backend = one site flag consumed by both webhook paths
N-05Import-from-GitHub front door — create-site entry: pick repo (list_repos) → framework auto-detect → content binding → site; templates become tab twoVercel "Import Git Repository" / Netlify "Import from Git"Both competitors open with import-from-git; our E-04 opens with templates. Post-gh-1 the import path is the growth wedge — merge F-01 into E-04 as the first tabGitHub App seam has list_repos; framework sniff is package.json reading; rest is the existing create flow
N-06DNS records editor — for domains delegated to a connected provider: A/CNAME/TXT table, upsert/delete, "managed by Barkpark" stateNetlify DNS (zone hosting)Closes the last mile of the domain story: today we checklist DNS but send users elsewhere to fix it; with a Hetzner/Cloudflare token connected we can just fix itDNS upsert/delete seams exist for both providers; needs list-records added to the seams
N-07Redirects editor — per-site ordered rules table (from → to → status), validated, applied on deployNetlify _redirects / Vercel vercel.json redirectsTable-stakes for real sites (moved pages, apex↔www, campaign URLs); absence forces users back into code for configNew: per-site rules blob rendered into the Caddy site block at deploy; small, contained

Concept sketches — the differentiators (N-08…N-10)

#ConceptModeled on — then invertedThe Barkpark twist
N-08Forms inbox — form submissions from hosted sites land as documents; console shows per-site inbox (new/seen, spam state, export)Netlify FormsSubmissions become type:form_submission documents in the bound dataset — queryable, schema-validated, visible in Studio, exportable via the content API. Netlify bolts an inbox onto hosting; we already ARE the content store. Likely the single strongest Netlify-parity move available to us
N-09Preview feedback → tasks — a lightweight comment affordance on preview sites; each comment files a bp task (screenshot, URL, viewport) linked to the deploymentVercel Comments / Netlify DrawerTheir comments die in the platform; ours land in the task system the team already works from (bp task, boards, claim queue). Collaboration parity without building a chat product
N-10Site analytics panel — per-site traffic: requests/s, bandwidth, p95, status-code split; Plausible embed when the template ships itNetlify Analytics / Vercel Web AnalyticsServer-side from Caddy logs on the box the user owns — no client JS, no cookie banner, honest "unmetered" when quiet. Requires per-site metering split (today meters are per-instance) — that's the real cost, hence sketch-first

Deliberate skips — confirmed anti-goals

• Functions / edge middleware / cron-as-product UI — no FaaS; the box is the compute story.
• Feature flags, Edge Config, split testing — needs edge logic we refuse; revisit only if cf_proxied grows programmable.
• Integrations marketplace — templates + providers are our integration surface.
• Domain registrar (buy domains) — connect-your-provider stays the model; reselling domains is a support burden with no identity payoff.
• Observability suite / log drains / APM — N-01's honest tail is the commitment; full observability is a different product.
• AI review / codegen consoles — out of scope for the hosting surface.

Sequencing against the build

N-02, N-04, N-05 belong to the auto-deploy design batch — same screens the designer just prototyped, request immediately as one package. N-01 and N-03 are standalone and high-identity-value — request now, build in phase 3/4. N-06/N-07 wait on small seam additions; request designs once those tasks are filed. N-08…N-10 go to the designer as concept briefs only after an owner call on whether Forms (N-08) enters the product — it is the one with real backend scope. Updated outline arithmetic: 51 → 61 surfaces (58 request-able now, 3 concept-gated).

The one-line strategy
Close on Vercel by finishing the git loop (already chartered); close on Netlify by taking Forms and Lock-production, which land better on a content platform than they do on Netlify; and refuse everything that would blur the named-box identity both competitors abstracted away.

Compiled 2026-07-18 against Netlify and Vercel console surfaces. Chain: 51-surface outline · Vercel gap analysis · auto-deploy target UI approved.
